name: 4D Block Geometry Slicing
definition: Blocks in the 4D world are 4D primitives (4-balls, 4-boxes). When sliced by the 3D hyperplane, they produce 3D cross-sections. A 4-ball (boulder) slice is a sphere with radius `sqrt(r² - d²)`, where `r` is the 4D radius and `d` is the distance from the 4D center to the hyperplane. A 4-box (monolith) slice footprint changes shape (e.g., rectangle to hexagon) as the cut angle changes.
summary: 4D Block Geometry Slicing renders 3D cross-sections of 4D voxel worlds by intersecting 4D primitives with a 3D hyperplane, allowing slice geometry to change shape as the hyperplane rotates or translates.
